meal.title: Printing messages and reading user input
meal.objective: Use print to display text and input to read user text

voice.script: What does print actually do? Imagine you want your program to talk. The print function sends whatever you give it to the screen, so the user can read it. Next, input lets the program pause and wait for the user to type something, returning that text as a string. Now let's see a tiny program. It prints a welcome line, then asks for your name with input, and finally prints a greeting that includes what you typed. When you run it, you’ll see the prompt and your reply echoed. Use print to show and input to receive user text. Try changing the prompt and printing a greeting.

scenes.narration_anchor: The print function sends whatever you give it to the screen, so the user can read it.

visual.code:
print("Welcome to the slot machine!")
name = input("Enter your name: ")
print("Hello, " + name + "! Ready to play?")
